title: Trading $20,000 with AI agents on Robinhood: what's working, what isn't
author: Unfair_Set_355
selftext:
Robinhood account: $20,399.51, up $211.58 (up 1.05%) today.



Whole book including the Kalshi and Coinbase sleeves: $21,014.34, up $288.56 (up 1.39%) today.



I started with $10,000 and added another $10,000 a couple of weeks ago once it was going well. Profit since the start, deposits taken out: up $323.63.



The strategies, and how they're doing:



The Kneeler (Kalshi, NFL). Late in games, once the leading team is running out the clock, it buys NO on stat lines that can't realistically be hit anymore. That's usually at 88 to 99 cents, and it collects the dollar at the final whistle. It's 89 for 89 across five game days. This Sunday was 11 for 11 and made $13.81. All time it's up $85 after fees on $644 put in.



FAANG+ Momentum ($5,155.79, up $112.36 today, best day in the book). Each morning it reranks the biggest tech names by short-term momentum and holds the leaders. Today it sold AAPL and GOOGL and bought AMZN and NVDA.



Business As Usual ($3,048.65, up $29.09). Holds the S&P 500, and switches into UPRO, a 3x leveraged S&P fund, on days New York weather reads normal for the season on Kalshi's temperature markets. Yes, really. Today was one of those days, so it bought UPRO at $148.44 at the open.



Full Send ($442.36, up 5.30% today). Holds TQQQ, the 3x Nasdaq fund, while the Nasdaq-100 is above its 200 day average, and Treasury bills otherwise. It's the most aggressive thing in the book, and days like today are why it's there.



AI Picks & Shovels ($883.70, up $27.07 today). Owns the AI buildout, chips through networking and power, reweighted by momentum. Today's reweight trimmed SMCI, ANET, DELL and some NVDA, and added AMD, MRVL and TSM.



Pelosi Tracker ($1,896.45, up $27.13, up 1.45%). It mirrors Nancy Pelosi's disclosed stock buys. Today it trimmed AAPL, AMZN and INTC and added Palo Alto Networks at $347.77 off her latest disclosure.



High Profile Congress ($488.57, up $2.85) does the same thing across a group of high volume Congress members. It swapped RARE, RIG, STAG and YETI for FITB, RPM and AT&T off a new filing.



FDA Inspector, down $7.45 today, the worst in the book. It sold its Amgen at $430.93 and bought Pfizer at $29.64. Its first Amgen buy in this run was $377.57.



Dip Buyer is easing new money into VOO only on dip days: about $300 at $704.93 today and a similar amount last Thursday. The rest of its $2,000 is still waiting for the next dip.



NFL Fantasy Agent buys YES on player props for my fantasy roster. It went 1 for 3 Sunday: Blake Corum 40+ rushing yards at 56 cents paid a dollar, while a Browns receiver touchdown and a CeeDee Lamb touchdown both went to zero. Still a lottery ticket and sized like one.
